faq_text: Agents, models, costs, compliance, formats, and deployment.
faq_what_answer: Ragmir is the retrieval layer for agentic RAG: it indexes selected project files and returns exact cited passages through TypeScript, CLI, or MCP. Your agent decides when to search again, reasons over the evidence, and generates the answer. Default retrieval works offline without a model download.
faq_private_question: Does Ragmir send my confidential code or documents?
faq_private_answer: Ragmir has no telemetry or hosted document store. It indexes on the machine where it runs and returns unmasked passages. Your chat or agent can forward those passages to a model provider. For confidential work, control the whole path: client, local or self-hosted model, connection, access, and logs. Optional semantic setup explicitly downloads model weights.
faq_agents_question: Which AI agents and tools does Ragmir work with?
faq_agents_answer: Ragmir Core is model-agnostic. Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and Cursor install it as a plugin, and Gemini CLI and Qwen Code as an extension, each with the retrieval skill and the MCP server. Kimi, OpenCode, and Cline connect through rgr setup. LangChain.js applications use RagmirRetriever or the agent tools, and Python applications install ragmir, langchain-ragmir for LangChain and LangGraph, or llama-index-retrievers-ragmir from PyPI. Any agent that loads skills installs the Ragmir skills with npx skills add jcode-works/ragmir, and coding assistants read the documentation on Context7. Other MCP clients, scripts, and CI jobs get the same cited results. Each server reads one project's base and warns or refuses unrelated workspaces.
faq_personal_question: Can I use Ragmir on personal documents, such as bank statements or my CV?
faq_personal_answer: Yes. Index the folders you choose: research and past transcripts for a YouTube script, a lifetime of paperwork, or your whole career history for a job search. Indexing and search run on your machine. Pair Ragmir with a local model such as Ollama to keep every passage there; with Claude Code, Codex, or Claude Desktop, the cited excerpts go to that provider.
faq_team_question: How does a team share the same knowledge base?
faq_team_answer: Commit a shared ragmir.config.json and share reviewed source documents through your normal Git or file-sharing workflow, then run rgr ingest on each workstation, or let rgr hooks install refresh the index after each pull. Each developer keeps a local index. Ragmir does not manage branches or synchronize peers.
faq_offline_question: Do I need an API key, a GPU, a vector database, or an internet connection?
faq_offline_answer: No. The default local-hash retrieval runs offline on the CPU, with no API key or model download, and the index is an embedded LanceDB store in the git-ignored .ragmir/ folder: there is no database server to run. Semantic retrieval adds the optional Transformers package and an explicit model download; it runs on the CPU, and ingestion can use a GPU through WebGPU. To reuse a model you already serve, the opt-in openai-compatible provider embeds through Ollama, vLLM, or another OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Ragmir itself is free under the AGPL-3.0: what remains is the machine it runs on and the model your agent calls.
faq_observability_question: Can I see where ingestion time and memory are spent?
faq_observability_answer: Optional ingestion metrics report phase timings, throughput, queues, OCR cache hits, and memory use. These local diagnostics omit document content and queries; there is no usage-tracking service.
faq_compare_question: How does Ragmir differ from an agent’s own search or a typical RAG pipeline?
faq_compare_answer: An agent’s own search matches exact words in text files and reads whole files into its context, which is often enough on a small code repository. Ragmir adds one local index for code, Office files, PDFs, and scans, a few compact citations per question, and no passage when the documents are silent. On Ragmir’s own repository, the right file reaches the top 3 for 83% of developer questions, against 79% for MiniSearch BM25 and 63% for a LangChain.js pipeline with the same embedding model, and Ragmir refuses 24 of 30 off-topic questions where they refuse at most 2. Unlike a hosted RAG, the index stays on your machine.
faq_role_question: Which model writes the answers, and can I change it later?
faq_role_answer: Your agent, chat, or application writes them with the model you choose; Ragmir only searches and cites. Claude, GPT, Gemini, Mistral, or a local model served by Ollama or vLLM read the same cited passages, so you can switch for cost, quality, or data residency without re-indexing. Only a new embedding model, which shapes the index itself, needs a rebuild. The integration guide covers local Ollama, self-hosted servers, and cloud providers.
faq_quality_question: How do I measure retrieval quality before going to production?
faq_quality_answer: Write a golden file of real questions with the files that should answer them, plus questions the documents must not answer. rgr evaluate reports recall, MRR, nDCG, citation accuracy, and the false-positive rate on those hard negatives, and exits with an error below your thresholds, so a CI job fails when retrieval regresses. --baseline prints the signed change against an earlier run, and the ragmir-evaluate skill walks an agent through the setup.
faq_compliance_question: Does Ragmir help with GDPR or the EU AI Act?
faq_compliance_answer: Ragmir is not legal advice and does not make a system compliant on its own. It helps you show how an answer was produced: the index stays on infrastructure you choose, you select the sources and credentials are left out, every passage cites its source, and evaluation reports document retrieval quality. Compliance also depends on the model, where it runs, who can access it, and what gets logged.
faq_wiki_question: Can my agent maintain a cited Markdown wiki with Ragmir?
faq_wiki_answer: Yes. In an LLM wiki, your agent writes the Markdown pages and Ragmir keeps them honest. Index the raw sources and the pages, cite each claim with a Ragmir citation, and list the sources in each page's front matter. rgr audit --knowledge then reports broken links, missing pages, changed citations, and pages whose sources changed, without editing anything. ragmir_expand shows a page's links and backlinks, and ragmir_sources with changedSince lists the files changed since the agent's last pass. The ragmir-wiki skill describes the routine and installs with npx skills add jcode-works/ragmir.
faq_formats_question: Which file formats can Ragmir index?
faq_formats_answer: More than 900 file types index with no extra install: source code in over 250 languages, text, Markdown, PDF, Word, PowerPoint, and Excel (macro-enabled files and templates included), OpenDocument, EPUB, HTML and saved web pages, CSV, JSON, YAML, translations, and build files such as Dockerfile. Exports are cited object by object: Figma, Sketch, Excalidraw, and tldraw frames; XMind sheets; emails, mailboxes, and Evernote notes; Postman and Insomnia requests and HAR captures; OpenAPI and AsyncAPI operations; PowerDesigner, ERwin, MySQL Workbench, draw.io, Visio, BPMN, ArchiMate, and UML models; Tableau and Power BI projects; GeoJSON features and SARIF findings. Scanned PDFs, photos, and legacy Word files can use optional local extractors, and unsupported files are flagged explicitly.
faq_server_question: Can Ragmir run on a VPS or a server without internet access?
faq_server_answer: Yes. Ragmir runs wherever Node.js 22.12 runs, including Debian and Alpine containers as a non-root user with a read-only filesystem and no network. It opens no HTTP port: agents reach it through stdio MCP, and your service embeds the TypeScript client and owns authentication, authorization, rate limits, and TLS. The official Docker image runs the CLI and MCP server without installing Node.js, and the server guide includes a working Dockerfile.

faq_license_question: Can I ship Ragmir inside a customer deployment or a commercial product?
faq_license_answer: Yes, under the AGPL-3.0 terms, which include offering the source of a modified version you distribute or run for users over a network. To integrate Ragmir into proprietary software or a hosted service without those obligations, JCode Works offers a separate commercial license.
